newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies giving military help to Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies giving military help to Sudan.

text.p: President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Wednesday Iran was reviewing a Sudanese request for military aid but denied it had given any.
"This is a lie. We have not recently given any military help to Sudan. They have made a request and we are reviewing it," Rafsanjani told a news conference.
He was responding to a question about reports that Iran had set up an airlift to send arms to Sudan.
"If one day we do help Sudan, nobody should complain because it is natural for two friendly countries to cooperate...We could sell them some things on a cash or a loan basis," he said.
"Our aid to Sudan up to now has been mostly humanitarian, such as oil or food," Rafsanjani added.
Tehran has close ties with Khartoum's Islamist government. Iran has condemned "all acts of aggression" in Sudan and supported the country's unity and territorial integrity.
Sudan has denied rebel reports that Iran has given the Sudanese army weapons, including banned chemical arms, cash and even troops.

Iranian media have accused the United States and Israel of conspiring to bring down the Khartoum government. Washington accuses both Tehran and Khartoum of sponsoring terrorism, a charge denied by the two countries.
Sudan says Ethiopia and Eritrea are behind the clashes in the east of the country. Both neighbouring states and the rebels deny this.
